title: Republicans Can’t Rely on Trump Voters Anymore

Republicans Can’t Rely on Trump Voters Anymore
Tim Carney, a senior political columnist at The Washington Examiner, argues that Trump’s voters never became reliably conservative and Republican. On “The Opinions,” he explains why “there’s no juice left to squeeze from MAGA” as Trump’s second term comes to an end.
- These people weren’t made into Paul Ryan acolytes who loved the idea of reforming Social Security. And frankly, they’re not the Ted Cruz vote from 2016. Remember, you could chart by county the places where people were more likely to go to church every week in the 2016 primaries — they were voting for Ted Cruz. The places where you had the White evangelicals who don’t attend church, they were more likely to be the Trump voter. So the less religiously observant, the less fiscally conservative — that was the Trump vote. And the Republicans cannot rely on them now that Trump is leaving the stage. And then you combine with that the fact that the party started selecting for loyalty to Trump rather than either conservatism or quality of candidate, and that also hurt the party. So going forward, the Republicans, there’s no juice left to squeeze from MAGA. And if anybody tries to be a mini MAGA, if JD Vance says, “I’m going to be the next Donald Trump” — You can’t be the next Donald Trump.
